newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sweet grades inch up on Cusiana tenders late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sweet grades inch up on Cusiana tenders late.

text.p: U.S. sweet grades inched up in thin cash activity late on Monday, reflecting the stronger-than-expected results of two Cusiana tenders, traders said.
June WTI/Cushing was trading around $19.60-70 a barrel, giving up some of the day's advances, but still up some five cents from late Friday's cash market on technical factors, traders said.
July WTI/Cushing was running around seven cents ahead of the June level, reinforcing the market contango in which forward prices exceed prompt ones.
Colombia's state oil company Ecopetrol sold two early June Cusiana cargoes to a pair of U.S. refiners for a discount of between $1.20 and $1.40 to WTI/Cushing on an fob basis.
The uptick in the Cusiana price was attributed to softening freight rates in the Caribbean.
U.S. domestic sweet grades felt the heat. Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was talked at WTI/Cushing minus 45-35 cents a barrel, up five cents from late Friday's cash market.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James picked up slightly from earlier talk at minus five to minus two cents, with minus three and minus four cents changing hands.
WTI/Midland was steady at minus 32-30 cents, with minus 31 transacted.
Sour grades were muted. West Texas Sour/Midland was around minus $1.73-70.
Eugene Island hovered at a discount of around $1.50-45.
WTI/Cushing Posting Plus was tighter at $1.80-82 a barrel, with $1.82 trading.
